check-in-counter.definition: A staffed airport desk where passengers confirm travel details and, when applicable, check baggage.
check-in-counter.exampleUsage: Omar presented his travel documents at the check-in counter.

boarding-pass.definition: A document or digital authorization used to board a flight under the carrier’s procedures.
boarding-pass.exampleUsage: The agent issued Omar a boarding pass after registration.

passport.definition: An official document that identifies a traveler and is used for international travel.
passport.exampleUsage: Omar showed his passport during the document check.

visa.definition: Official permission to enter or stay in a country under specified conditions.
visa.exampleUsage: The visa has stated conditions and does not guarantee entry in every circumstance.

luggage.definition: Cases used to carry belongings when traveling.
luggage.exampleUsage: Omar packed his luggage before leaving home.

suitcase.definition: A portable rectangular container for carrying clothes.
suitcase.exampleUsage: He put his clothes in a suitcase.

carry-on.definition: A small bag or item that a passenger is permitted to take into the aircraft cabin under airline rules.
carry-on.exampleUsage: His carry-on meets the airline's stated cabin-baggage requirements.

baggage-claim.definition: An airport area where passengers retrieve luggage unloaded from an arriving aircraft.
baggage-claim.exampleUsage: Omar collected his checked bag at baggage claim.

conveyor-belt.definition: A moving belt that carries luggage through the airport.
conveyor-belt.exampleUsage: The conveyor belt carried the bags through the screening area.

security-check.definition: An airport screening process used to check passengers and belongings for prohibited or unsafe items.
security-check.exampleUsage: Passengers followed staff directions at the security check.

metal-detector.definition: A screening device that detects metal carried by a person or in belongings.
metal-detector.exampleUsage: The metal detector was part of the screening equipment.

scanner.definition: A machine used to examine passengers or baggage during security screening.
scanner.exampleUsage: The scanner examined baggage during the security process.

terminal.definition: An airport building where passengers check in, arrive, or leave.

gate.definition: Passageway (as in an air terminal) where passengers can embark or disembark.
gate.exampleUsage: The boarding announcement directed passengers to the assigned gate.

runway.definition: A long prepared surface where aircraft take off and land.
runway.exampleUsage: The aircraft landed on the runway.

control-tower.definition: A raised, glass-enclosed workplace at an airport lets controllers watch aircraft as they arrive, depart, and move nearby.
control-tower.exampleUsage: Controllers coordinate aircraft movements from the control tower.

hangar.definition: A large structure at an airport where aircraft can be stored and maintained.
hangar.exampleUsage: The aircraft was stored in the hangar during maintenance.

departure-lounge.definition: A waiting area where air travelers stay until their scheduled flight departs.
departure-lounge.exampleUsage: Omar waited in the departure lounge.

arrivals-hall.definition: The airport area where arriving passengers enter after leaving baggage claim or border-control areas.
arrivals-hall.exampleUsage: Relatives waited in the arrivals hall.

duty-free-shop.definition: A shop in an international travel area where certain goods may be sold without some local taxes or duties under applicable rules.
duty-free-shop.exampleUsage: The duty-free shop sells eligible goods under specific tax rules.

food-court.definition: An area with several food outlets and shared seating.
food-court.exampleUsage: Omar bought lunch at the food court.

restroom.definition: A public room containing toilets and washing facilities.
restroom.exampleUsage: He asked a staff member for the nearest restroom.

elevator.definition: Lifting device consisting of a platform or cage that is raised and lowered mechanically in a vertical shaft in order to move people from one floor to another in a building.
elevator.exampleUsage: The elevator carried passengers to another floor.

escalator.definition: A stairway whose steps move continuously on a circulating belt.
escalator.exampleUsage: The escalator connects two levels of the terminal.

airplane.definition: An aircraft that has a fixed wing and is powered by propellers or jets.
airplane.exampleUsage: The airplane carries passengers between the two airports.

jet-engine.definition: An engine that propels aircraft or missiles by burning fuel and forcing high-speed exhaust gases backward.
jet-engine.exampleUsage: The jet engine produces thrust through its exhaust flow.

wing.definition: One of the horizontal airfoils on either side of the fuselage of an airplane.
wing.exampleUsage: The aircraft's wing extends from the fuselage.

cockpit.definition: Compartment where the pilot sits while flying the aircraft.
cockpit.exampleUsage: The pilot worked in the cockpit.

fuselage.definition: The central body of an airplane that is designed to accommodate the crew and passengers (or cargo).
fuselage.exampleUsage: The fuselage contains the passenger cabin.

propeller.definition: A mechanical device that rotates to push against air or water.
propeller.exampleUsage: The propeller rotated to produce thrust in the compatible aircraft.

tail.definition: The rear part of an aircraft that helps keep it stable.
tail.exampleUsage: The aircraft's tail assembly is at its rear.

landing-gear.definition: A set of fixed or retractable supports on an aircraft or spacecraft cushions touchdown and keeps the vehicle stable during takeoff, landing, and movement on the ground.
landing-gear.exampleUsage: The landing gear supports the aircraft on the ground.

window.definition: A transparent opening in an aircraft through which passengers can see outside.
window.exampleUsage: Omar looked through the aircraft window.

aisle.definition: Passageway between seating areas as in an auditorium or passenger vehicle or between areas of shelves of goods as in stores.
aisle.exampleUsage: The aisle runs between the rows of seats.

overhead-bin.definition: A storage compartment above passenger seats in an aircraft cabin.
overhead-bin.exampleUsage: The crew checked that the overhead bin was closed.

tray-table.definition: A small folding table attached to or near an aircraft seat.
tray-table.exampleUsage: The tray table was folded under crew instructions.

pilot.definition: A person trained to fly and control an aircraft.

co-pilot.definition: A qualified pilot who shares aircraft-operating duties with the captain and can take control when required.
co-pilot.exampleUsage: The co-pilot reviewed flight information with the captain.

flight-attendant.definition: A trained crew member responsible for passenger safety and service in an aircraft cabin.
flight-attendant.exampleUsage: The flight attendant explained the cabin safety information.

passenger.definition: A traveler riding in a vehicle (a boat or bus or car or plane or train etc.) who is not operating it.
passenger.exampleUsage: The passenger took the assigned seat.

ground-crew.definition: Airport workers who service aircraft, handle baggage, or support flights on the ground.
ground-crew.exampleUsage: The ground crew prepared the aircraft for its next flight.

air-traffic-controller.definition: A trained professional who directs and coordinates aircraft movements to maintain safe separation.
air-traffic-controller.exampleUsage: The air traffic controller communicated with arriving aircraft.

customs-officer.definition: A government official who enforces rules about goods entering or leaving a country.
customs-officer.exampleUsage: The customs officer checked the goods declaration.

immigration-officer.definition: A government official who checks travelers' documents and entry or exit status at a border.
immigration-officer.exampleUsage: The immigration officer examined the traveler's passport.

baggage-handler.definition: An airport worker who loads, unloads, sorts, or moves passengers' baggage.
baggage-handler.exampleUsage: The baggage handler moved suitcases onto the cart.

mechanic.definition: A skilled worker who maintains and repairs aircraft.
mechanic.exampleUsage: The mechanic inspected the aircraft during authorized maintenance.

boarding.definition: The act of passengers and crew getting aboard a ship or aircraft.
boarding.exampleUsage: Boarding started after the gate announcement.

takeoff.definition: The moment when an aircraft leaves the ground and begins to fly.
takeoff.exampleUsage: The aircraft left the runway during takeoff.

landing.definition: The act of coming down to the earth (or other surface).
landing.exampleUsage: The aircraft reached the runway during landing.

taxiing.definition: The movement of an aircraft along the ground under its own power before takeoff or after landing.
taxiing.exampleUsage: The aircraft was taxiing toward the assigned ground position.

turbulence.definition: Irregular air movement that can make an aircraft shake.
turbulence.exampleUsage: The flight encountered turbulence in the air.

announcement.exampleUsage: The announcement gave passengers current departure information.

fasten-seatbelt.definition: To secure a seat belt by connecting its buckle and adjusting it as required by the transport operator.
fasten-seatbelt.exampleUsage: The crew asked passengers to fasten their seatbelt.

emergency-exit.definition: A clearly marked doorway or route allows people to evacuate quickly when fire, collapse, or another serious threat occurs.
emergency-exit.exampleUsage: The crew pointed out the emergency exit.

life-vest.definition: A sleeveless jacket designed to keep a person afloat during an emergency in water.
life-vest.exampleUsage: The life vest is part of the aircraft's emergency equipment.

oxygen-mask.definition: A mask delivering supplemental oxygen from the aircraft’s relevant oxygen system.
oxygen-mask.exampleUsage: The oxygen mask supplies supplemental oxygen through the relevant aircraft system.

delay.definition: A later arrival or departure than the scheduled time.
delay.exampleUsage: The delay moved departure later than the scheduled time.

layover.definition: A stop between flights during a journey.
layover.exampleUsage: Omar had a layover between his connecting flights.
